summaries.demographer: Hanh Gunasekara is a 51-year-old married Vietnamese American woman living in Bel Air, Maryland, with her husband Ruwan and no children in the household (Q05, Q11, Q84). She was born in Silver Spring, grew up in Rockville with both immigrant parents and a younger sister, and identifies as Asian, Vietnamese American, and culturally Buddhist (Q86-Q99). She has an MBA and works full time as a financial manager, placing her in a stable upper-middle-income professional household with homeownership, employer benefits, and substantial savings (Q58, Q65, Q72-Q83). Her life course reflects second-generation immigrant mobility, graduate education, stable marriage, and active elder-care obligations for her mother (Q35, Q90).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Hanh shows high planning capacity, delayed gratification, and strong precautionary saving, with emergency funds, retirement accounts, sinking funds, and low consumer debt (Q61-Q64, Q82-Q83). Her choices are motivated by stability, competence, and option value rather than conspicuous consumption, though she allows bounded indulgences in travel, concerts, food, and vintage kitchen gadgets (Q56-Q60, Q108-Q109). She responds to uncertainty by creating structure but prefers flexible implementation, as seen in her career crossroads, household budgeting, and hybrid work routines (Q02-Q03, Q17, Q78). Her risk posture is calculated rather than avoidant: she accepted a difficult systems role because it increased long-run career capital (Q02).
summaries.political_scientist: Hanh is a regular voter and moderate Democrat who is center-left on social policy, democracy, climate, health care, immigration, and racial justice while retaining a professional concern for fiscal discipline and competent implementation (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). Her civic identity is shaped by immigrant family citizenship norms and practical trust in institutions that function well, including schools, libraries, public health, and local government (Q23-Q24). She supports police accountability and racial equity reforms but tends toward dialogue, donations, workplace influence, and institutional change rather than protest politics (Q26-Q30). Her political style is pragmatic, data-oriented, and wary of misinformation and performative partisanship (Q24-Q25, Q48).
summaries.psychologist: Hanh presents as conscientious, analytical, reserved, culturally grounded, and quietly ambitious, with a self-concept built around competence, steadiness, family duty, and adaptability (Q01-Q04, Q109). She regulates stress through practical systems, lists, hiking, cooking, yoga, reading, meditation, and support from her husband, sister, and close friends (Q43-Q50). She reports mild anxiety rather than clinical depression, with stress clustering around work transformation, elder care, and open-ended responsibility (Q44-Q46). Relationally, she prefers a small dependable circle and expresses care through tasks, financial help, translation, cooking, and planning, reflecting both personality and immigrant-family norms (Q05-Q07, Q35, Q109).
